status: NORMATIVE_DRAFT — binding for every program-owned repository from R00 (DEC-AUP-0008); provisional receipts written before this schema (e.g. receipts/acceptance/change-admission-20260905T064425Z.json) are asserted, not validated (I14)
purpose: The receipt is the admission gate: it proves which graph (commit, digest, freshness) selected the verification, what changed, what the graph predicted as affected (with the provenance of every path), which verifiers actually ran with their outputs, and a tri-valued verdict for every affected entity. A receipt cannot be issued on a stale graph; an empty impact set on a non-documentation change must be explained; exemptions need an owner and an expiry.
charter_rule_text: Проверка изменения кода по умолчанию — graph-verified change: обновить/проверить свежесть графа связей, вычислить множество влияния, исполнить обязательные верификаторы для каждой затронутой сущности, выдать receipt с тривалентными вердиктами. Тесты — выбираемый верификатор, TDD — opt-in клиентских пространств. Граф выбирает проверку, он её не заменяет: пустое множество влияния — предсказание, требующее объяснения, не одобрение.

staleness.rule: verdict fresh requires graph.source_commit == tree.commit (worktree mode) or == change_set.base (diff mode), tree.dirty consistent with change_set.mode, and 0 mismatched_nodes

empty_impact_explanation.graph_metadata: which extractors ran, language coverage, and why the changed nodes have no reverse edges (e.g. leaf unit, new file, unsupported language); an explanation may not simply say 'no impact'

binding.rule: Optional author input is exact-revision/digest bound to both independently rebuilt graphs. Raw EMPTY_IMPACT_REQUIRES_EXPLANATION events remain unchanged. Only the empty dependent prediction diagnostic is satisfied; ordinary seed/verifier obligations, other diagnostics, failed/not_measured results and additive full-global obligations remain. The native gate independently reproduces all metadata and the input digest; no verdict, waiver, disable or exemption field is accepted. A new confirmed explanation carries schema BoundEmptyImpactExplanation/v1; removing its binding is refused. Legacy generated/unconfirmed explanation documents remain readable with their original raw query diagnostics and do not acquire confirmation.

verdict.rule: every impact entry (core and tail) and every changed node has exactly one verdict; verified requires ≥ 1 verifier_id; not_measured requires a reason

exemption.rule: owner is a role or person from the registry, never empty; expires_at_utc must be after captured_at_utc

admission.rule: admitted requires every verdict = verified; admitted_with_exemptions requires every non-verified entity to have an unexpired exemption; failed without exemption ⇒ refused; not_measured without exemption ⇒ paused_safe or refused

head_graph.rule: If paired evidence is present: source_commit equals change_set.head, sha256 digest is exact rebuilt head graph, staleness.verdict is fresh.

caller_graph_compatibility.rule: Optional paired diff binding only. Primary graph/head_graph are genuine outputs of the unchanged canonical-path signed BASE caller bundle, trusted under the current producer's canonical public key. Independently rebuild installed and current graphs at both exact Git revisions. Entire graph documents must agree except genuine builder_version, built_at_utc and graph_digest; all other manifest fields, nodes, edges and attributes participate. Record both actual digests and versions, semantic body hash and the actual current producer source-file digest. The gate independently reproduces this binding before ordinary impact, mandatory verifier, raw verdict and full-fallback checks; it grants no exemption. No graph header/digest rewrite, arbitrary executable/path or version-only compatibility. Absent binding retains ordinary current-producer admission.

revision_selection.rule: Entity arrays come from separate revision traversals. Every base/head entity requires a verdict; native required_by_entity must cover them. Unmeasured head code prohibits admission. Gate independently recomputes from Git.

structural_exclusions.note: DEC-AUP-0034. Affected entities that owe this change no verdict: the verifier matrix declares neither a mandatory nor a selectable verifier for their node type (`receipt`, `work_item` today), the change set does not contain them, and their bytes are identical at base and head. Each entry carries the content hash at both revisions that proves the byte-identity, and impact_pair.receipt_problems re-derives every condition from Git before it counts the entity as covered. An entity that fails any condition keeps its ordinary tri-valued verdict — editing a receipt is an ordinary change to a file. This is NOT an exemption: an exemption carries an owner and an expiry because it is a debt, and there is nothing here to repay. DEC-AUP-0035 adds a SECOND, separately identified class, marked `rule: DEC-AUP-0035` and carrying a `superseded` block: the previous version of THIS receipt, at the path this run writes to (`receipt_path`), declaring the same `work_item`. That entity IS in the change set and its bytes DO differ — the two facts DEC-AUP-0034 relies on are inverted — so it is admitted on entirely different evidence: impact_pair re-derives the path, the work item declared by the blob at each revision, and the digests, and refuses anything else. `content_hash` may name only one revision (null at the other) because a receipt filed inside the range does not exist at base. Without it, re-issuing a receipt after a rebase pauses the change on the record of itself — hand-written expiring exemptions had to cover that on ARAS #195 and #196.

superseded.rule: work_item must equal the receipt's own work_item and receipt_path must equal both the entry's path and the receipt's receipt_path; every version of that file existing at base or head must parse as a *Receipt/v1 declaring the same work item.

receipt_path.note: DEC-AUP-0035. The path, relative to the repository, that this receipt was written to (`verify.py --out` inside the tree; absent when it is written outside). It is the anchor of a superseded-self exclusion: a claim that an entity is «the previous version of me» is checkable only against the path this document actually occupies, and admit_change.py compares this field with where it FOUND the receipt.

observed.note: DEC-AUP-0039. The measurement an endpoint probe makes is of a RUNNING contour, so unlike a type-check it cannot be re-derived from the tree at head: whoever reads the receipt later has only what the receipt carries. This section IS that evidence, one row per probe — what was asked, what shape was expected, what was observed, a tri-valued verdict, and which run produced it. Before this section existed, A2-251 wrote its fifteen probe results into an `observed` key the validator tolerated and no rule read: a receipt every one of whose observations had failed was still `conformant` (measured on program 574fd08). A section nobody's verdict rests on claims nothing, so the binding is explicit and one-directional: a row names the `verifier_id` of the `endpoint_probe` row it belongs to, and that verifier row is the ONLY path by which a probe can support an entity's verdict. Granularity is the verifier row, not the probe: a claim that some of its probes were green and others were not is two claims and needs two rows. An honest `not_measured` probe is conformant and must stay conformant — what is refused is CASHING it as `verified`.
observed.rule: probe ids are unique within the receipt; verifier_id names a verifier of this receipt whose kind is endpoint_probe; a row whose verdict is failed or not_measured carries a detail saying what was seen instead (the tri-valued discipline of verdict.rule, applied one level down)

verifier_selection.rule: A2-413. What was asked for (`requested`, the --select set, [] when nothing), what applied to which entity (`applied`: verifier → entities), and why a requested verifier did not apply (`not_applied`: verifier, reason, entities). Every requested verifier is accounted for in applied or not_applied; applied keys and not_applied verifiers are requested ones; when `verify.required_by_entity` is present, an entity is listed under applied[v] exactly when v is in its required set. The prose `selected:` note in `notes`, when present, must name the same set. Absent on receipts from producers that predate it — their silence is a dated fact, never backfilled — and required from tools/graph/verify.py >= 1.1.0.

rules.RECEIPT_MISSING_FIELD: a required top-level or nested field is absent
rules.RECEIPT_WITHOUT_GRAPH_COMMIT: graph.source_commit absent or not a 40-hex sha
rules.RECEIPT_WITHOUT_GRAPH_DIGEST: graph.graph_digest absent or not sha256:<64 hex>
rules.RECEIPT_ON_STALE_GRAPH: staleness.verdict ≠ fresh, or graph.source_commit ≠ the commit the change set is measured against, or tree.dirty in diff mode, or mismatched_nodes non-empty
rules.STALENESS_NOT_CHECKED: staleness.verdict = not_checked (a receipt cannot be issued without the check)
rules.CHANGE_SET_FILE_INVALID: a change_set file lacks path/status/kind or uses a value outside the enums
rules.EMPTY_IMPACT_WITHOUT_EXPLANATION: deterministic_core and inferred_tail are both empty, global_fallback not triggered, at least one changed file is not kind doc/receipt, and empty_impact_explanation is absent or lacks graph_metadata
rules.IMPACT_ENTRY_WITHOUT_PROVENANCE: an impact entry path hop lacks provenance, or an entry has an empty path
rules.IMPACT_ENTRY_MISPLACED: an entry whose path contains an inferred/observed hop sits in deterministic_core, or a fully deterministic path sits in inferred_tail
rules.INFERRED_BOUNDARY_WITHOUT_CANARY: an impact entry reached through an inferred/observed hop with boundary = service (or repo) has no verifier of kind canary listing it and no valid exemption, while its verdict is verified or the admission verdict is admitted/admitted_with_exemptions (an honest not_measured with paused_safe/refused is conformant)
rules.VERIFIER_WITHOUT_OUTPUT_REF: a verifier lacks output_ref (path/URL of the captured output) or exit_code
rules.ENTITY_WITHOUT_VERDICT: an impact entry or changed node has no verdict
rules.VERDICT_NOT_TRIVALUED: a verdict value outside {verified, failed, not_measured} (booleans, pass/fail, ok, skipped are all violations)
rules.VERIFIED_WITHOUT_VERIFIER: verdict verified with no verifier_ids or with an id that names no verifier
rules.EXEMPTION_WITHOUT_OWNER: exemption lacks owner (or owner is empty)
rules.EXEMPTION_WITHOUT_EXPIRY: exemption lacks expires_at_utc or it is not ISO-8601 UTC
rules.ADMISSION_CONTRADICTS_VERDICTS: admission.verdict admitted with a failed/not_measured verdict; admitted_with_exemptions with a non-verified entity lacking a valid exemption; admitted while global_fallback triggered without every entity verified
rules.HEAD_GRAPH_BINDING_INVALID: Paired receipt has missing/invalid head revision, digest or freshness.
rules.REVISION_SELECTION_INCOMPLETE: Paired selection malformed or selected entities omitted from verdict/required mapping, or unmeasured head code admitted.
rules.STRUCTURAL_EXCLUSION_INVALID: a structural_exclusions entry is malformed, carries a content_hash that is not one equal sha256:<64 hex> at base and head (DEC-AUP-0034) or not a sha256/null pair naming at least one revision (DEC-AUP-0035), names an entity that also has a verdict, names an entity the change set contains (DEC-AUP-0034), or claims supersession of a path that is not this receipt's own receipt_path or of a work item that is not this receipt's own (DEC-AUP-0035)
rules.CANARY_CLAIM_WITHOUT_COMMITTED_EVIDENCE: DEC-AUP-0037: a verifier of kind canary whose output_ref is not a repository-relative path (absolute path, URL, or a path escaping the repository) while some entity CASHES that claim — a verdict of verified citing the verifier id, or the verifier being what keeps INFERRED_BOUNDARY_WITHOUT_CANARY quiet for a boundary entity. Evidence the gate cannot open at the receipt's head is testimony, not measurement; the entities a canary covers are the ones its document lists, never the ones the receipt's verifier row lists.
rules.OBSERVED_ENTRY_INVALID: an `observed` row is malformed: it is not an object, lacks probe/verifier_id/expected/observed/verdict/source, carries a verdict outside {verified, failed, not_measured}, repeats a probe id, omits `detail` on a failed/not_measured row, or names a verifier_id that is not a verifier of kind endpoint_probe in this receipt
rules.ENDPOINT_PROBE_WITHOUT_OBSERVATION: a verifier of kind endpoint_probe that some entity CASHES — a `verified` verdict cites it — while no `observed` row names it: a claim of measurement with no measurement recorded. A probe row nothing rests on claims nothing and is not reported, the same `cashed` condition DEC-AUP-0037 applies to a canary
rules.PROBE_CLAIM_CONTRADICTS_OBSERVATION: an entity whose verdict is `verified` cites a verifier of kind endpoint_probe among whose `observed` rows at least one carries verdict failed or not_measured — the receipt claims more than the contour was observed to do. An exemption cannot waive this: an exemption is the instrument for a NON-verified entity, and this rule fires precisely where the receipt says `verified`. The honest shapes are a `not_measured`/`failed` verdict for the entity, or a second endpoint_probe row that carries only the probes that were green
rules.VERIFIER_SELECTION_INVALID: verifier_selection is malformed or contradicts itself or verify.required_by_entity: unknown schema/verifier/reason, an applied or not_applied verifier that was not requested, a requested verifier accounted for nowhere, or an applied set that disagrees with the required set
rules.VERIFIER_SELECTION_MISSING: a receipt from a producer that writes verifier_selection (tools/graph/verify.py >= 1.1.0) carries none — the absence that cannot be told apart from «nobody asked»
rules.VERIFIER_SELECTION_CONTRADICTS_NOTES: the prose `selected:` note and verifier_selection.requested name different sets
